In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence that antiretroviral therapy (ART) is safe and effective for pregnant women with HIV infection.
there is no clear evidence that antiretroviral therapy in pregnancy reduces the risk of transmission of HIV from mother to child.
The evidence is not sufficient to determine the effectiveness of the use of antiretrovirals during the periconception period and pregnancy in preventing perinatal transmission of HIV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the treatment of maternal HIV disease is essential to the health of the infant.
we have demonstrated that the use of antiretroviral drugs during pregnancy can prevent HIV transmission from mother to child.
we have shown the potential of the use of the antiretroviral drugs for the prevention and treatment of the HIV/AIDS.

the antiretroviral drugs that are available today are very safe for pregnant women and very safe for the babies.
